svg.title: Horizontal asymptotes and how fast functions grow
svg.desc: Left: the graph of f(x) = (2x² + x)/(x² + 1) for x from −10 to 10 with the dashed horizontal asymptote y = 2. The graph crosses the asymptote at x = 2 and then approaches it from above, so a graph may cross a horizontal asymptote. Right: ln x in green, x³ in blue and eˣ in crimson for x from 0 to 6. At first x³ is above eˣ, but eˣ passes it near x = 4.54 and stays ahead; ln x grows slowest.
svg.text: Left: a finite limit at infinity gives a horizontal asymptote. Right: ex eventually beats any power of x; ln x loses to every power.
